svg.title: The em staircase and the cobweb
svg.desc: Left: for a single observation y = 1.8 of the symmetric two-component mixture, contours of the divergence F(a, m) between a point a of the data manifold D and a point m of the model manifold M, the sigmoid curve of the E-step, the straight line of the M-step and the staircase of the em algorithm descending to the minimum near m = 1.79; the point m = 0 is a stationary point that is not a minimum. Right: the EM map of the symmetric mixture for true separations m = 0.5 and 1.5 with cobwebs from m = 2.6; the slope at the fixed point is 0.657 and 0.084.
svg.text: One observation y = 1.8: the two projections
true m = 0.5: slope 0.657 at the fixed point
Left: F(a, m) is the divergence between the point a of D and the point m of M. The E-step moves vertically to
the curve a = σ(2my), the M-step horizontally to the straight line m = (2a − 1)y; the staircase reaches the
minimum (orange dot). The grey dot, m = 0, is stationary but not a minimum: EM started exactly there stays.
Right: the same algorithm on many observations, as a map m → m'; its slope at the fixed point is the speed.
